newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end up after shekel's decline.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end up after shekel's decline.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked and dollar-linked bonds closed higher on Sunday following the sharp rise of the dollar on Friday, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.13 pct to 108.79
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.11 pct to 108.48
* Unlinked government bonds: -0.03 pct to 109.32
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.73 pct to 110.25
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 107.55
Volume including Makams was 151 million shekels.

"The dollar is driving the market crazy," said Danny Shamir at Israel Discount Bank. "After the sharp rise of the dollar on Friday, investors started running to CPI-linked-bonds and dollar-linked bonds."
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5530 shekels on Friday against 3.5170 on Thursday.
Shamir said that investors bought inflation-linked bonds believing that a stronger dollar would lead to higher inflation.
"The market continues to be very nervous as the forex market is very volatile," Shamir said.
Most of the activity, he said, was concentrated in unlinked bombs.

"Some investors used the opportunity today to buy unlinked bonds as they predict that the dollar will stabilise at 3.5 shekels. Others, however, sold these bonds because they think that higher inflation will lead to a rate hike," Shamir said.
Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House said that the market was expected to stabilise soon.
"In the near term the market will remain at the current level. But in the long term it is expected to continue rising with falling yields," he said.
Weisberg added that yields on CPI-linked bonds were expected to fall below four percent from the current 4.05 percent.
"The government will issue less bonds in the future and this will lead to higher demand," he said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1=3.55 shekels)
